'''Adi Shamir''' ({{langx|he|עדי שמיר}}; born July 6, 1952) is an Israeli [[cryptography|cryptographer]] and inventor. He is a co-inventor of the [[RSA (algorithm)|Rivest–Shamir–Adleman]] (RSA) [[algorithm]] (along with [[Ron Rivest]] and [[Len Adleman]]), a co-inventor of the [[Feige–Fiat–Shamir identification scheme]] (along with [[Uriel Feige]] and [[Amos Fiat]]), one of the inventors of [[differential cryptanalysis]] and has made numerous contributions to the fields of [[cryptography]] and [[computer science]].<ref name=dblp>{{DBLP}}</ref> In 2002, [[Ron Rivest]], [[Len Adleman]], and Shamir won the ACM [[Turing Award]].<ref name=":0" />

==Early life and education==
Adi Shamir was born in [[Tel Aviv]]. He  received a [[Bachelor of Science]] (BSc) degree in [[mathematics]] from [[Tel Aviv University]] in 1973 and obtained an [[Master of Science|MSc]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in [[computer science]] from the [[Weizmann Institute]] in 1975 and 1977 respectively.<ref name=mathgene>{{MathGenealogy}}</ref> He spent a year as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] at the [[University of Warwick]] and did research at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) from 1977 to 1980.
==Scientific career==
In 1980, he returned to Israel, joining the faculty of [[Mathematics]] and [[Computer Science]] at the [[Weizmann Institute]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Adi Shamir - A.M. Turing Award Laureate |url=https://amturing.acm.org/award_winners/shamir_2327856.cfm |access-date=2026-07-13 |website=amturing.acm.org}}</ref> Starting from 2006, he is also an invited professor at [[École Normale Supérieure]] in Paris.<ref name=":3" />

In addition to [[RSA (algorithm)|RSA]], Shamir's other numerous inventions and contributions to cryptography include the [[Shamir's Secret Sharing|Shamir secret sharing]] scheme, the breaking of the [[Merkle-Hellman knapsack cryptosystem]], [[visual cryptography]], and the [[TWIRL]] and [[TWINKLE]] [[integer factorization|factoring]] devices. Together with [[Eli Biham]], he discovered [[differential cryptanalysis]] in the late 1980s, a general method for attacking [[block cipher]]s. It later emerged that differential cryptanalysis was already known — and kept a secret — by both [[IBM]]<ref name="coppersmith">{{cite journal |doi = 10.1147/rd.383.0243 |last = Coppersmith |first = Don |date = May 1994 |title = The Data Encryption Standard (DES) and its strength against attacks |journal = IBM Journal of Research and Development |volume = 38 |issue = 3 |pages = 243–250 |url = http://www.research.ibm.com/journal/rd/383/coppersmith.pdf |url-status = live |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070615132907/http://www.research.ibm.com/journal/rd/383/coppersmith.pdf |archive-date = 2007-06-15 }} (subscription required)</ref> and the [[National Security Agency]] (NSA).<ref name="levy">{{cite book |last = Levy |first = Steven |author-link = Steven Levy |title = Crypto: How the Code Rebels Beat the Government — Saving Privacy in the Digital Age |publisher = [[Penguin Books]] |year = 2001 |isbn = 0-14-024432-8 |pages = 55–56 }}</ref>

In 1984, Shamir introduced the concept of [[identity-based cryptography]], in which a user's public key can be derived from a unique identifier such as an email address.<ref>{{cite book |last=Shamir |first=Adi |title=Advances in Cryptology – CRYPTO 1984 |publisher=Springer |year=1985 |isbn=978-3-540-15658-1 |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=196 |pages=47–53 |chapter=Identity-Based Cryptosystems and Signature Schemes |doi=10.1007/3-540-39568-7_5}}</ref>

In 1986, together with [[Amos Fiat]], he devised the [[Fiat–Shamir heuristic]], a widely used method for converting interactive [[Identification protocol|identification protocols]] into [[digital signature]] schemes.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Fiat |first1=Amos |title=Advances in Cryptology – CRYPTO' 86 |last2=Shamir |first2=Adi |publisher=Springer |year=1987 |isbn=978-3-540-18047-0 |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=263 |pages=186–194 |chapter=How To Prove Yourself: Practical Solutions to Identification and Signature Problems |doi=10.1007/3-540-47721-7_12}}</ref>

Together with Rivest and Adleman, Shamir co-founded [[RSA Security]], the company behind the annual [[RSA Conference]] held since 1991.<ref name=":2">{{cite web |last=Thomson |first=Iain |date=March 5, 2019 |title=Adi Shamir visa snub: US govt slammed after the S in RSA blocked from his own RSA conf |url=https://www.theregister.com/2019/03/05/rsa_cofounder_us_visa_row/ |access-date=July 13, 2026 |website=[[The Register]]}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

With [[Alex Biryukov]] and David Wagner, he presented in 2000 a real-time cryptanalysis of [[A5/1]], the [[stream cipher]] used to encrypt [[GSM]] mobile phone communications.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Biryukov |first1=Alex |title=Fast Software Encryption – FSE 2000 |last2=Shamir |first2=Adi |last3=Wagner |first3=David |publisher=Springer |year=2001 |isbn=978-3-540-41728-6 |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=1978 |pages=1–18 |chapter=Real Time Cryptanalysis of A5/1 on a PC |doi=10.1007/3-540-44706-7_1}}</ref>

In 2001, with [[Ron Rivest]] and Yael Tauman, he introduced the concept of [[Ring signature|ring signatures]], which allow a member of a group to sign a message without revealing which member produced the signature.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Rivest |first1=Ronald L. |title=Advances in Cryptology – ASIACRYPT 2001 |last2=Shamir |first2=Adi |last3=Tauman |first3=Yael |publisher=Springer |year=2001 |isbn=978-3-540-42987-6 |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=2248 |pages=552–565 |chapter=How to Leak a Secret |doi=10.1007/3-540-45682-1_32}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite web |title=Adi Shamir |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/adi-shamir |access-date=July 13, 2026 |website=American Academy of Arts and Sciences}}</ref> The same year, together with Scott Fluhrer and Itsik Mantin, he published a key-recovery attack on the [[RC4]] stream cipher, known as the [[Fluhrer, Mantin and Shamir attack|Fluhrer–Mantin–Shamir attack]], which demonstrated a practical weakness in the [[Wired Equivalent Privacy]] (WEP) protocol then used to secure [[Wi-Fi]] networks.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Fluhrer |first1=Scott |title=Selected Areas in Cryptography – SAC 2001 |last2=Mantin |first2=Itsik |last3=Shamir |first3=Adi |publisher=Springer |year=2001 |isbn=978-3-540-43066-7 |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=2259 |pages=1–24 |chapter=Weaknesses in the Key Scheduling Algorithm of RC4 |doi=10.1007/3-540-45537-X_1}}</ref>

Shamir has also developed a range of [[Side-channel attack|side-channel attacks]] on cryptographic implementations, including cache attacks and [[acoustic cryptanalysis]]; in 2014, together with Daniel Genkin and [[Eran Tromer]], he demonstrated the extraction of full 4096-bit RSA keys from a laptop using the sound it emits during decryption.<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Adi Shamir FRS |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/adi-shamir-13842/ |access-date=July 13, 2026 |publisher=[[Royal Society]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Genkin |first1=Daniel |title=Advances in Cryptology – CRYPTO 2014 |last2=Shamir |first2=Adi |last3=Tromer |first3=Eran |publisher=Springer |year=2014 |isbn=978-3-662-44370-5 |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=8616 |pages=444–461 |chapter=RSA Key Extraction via Low-Bandwidth Acoustic Cryptanalysis |doi=10.1007/978-3-662-44371-2_25}}</ref>

Since the late 2010s, Shamir has also studied the security of [[machine learning]] systems, co-authoring work on the theory of adversarial examples, including the "Dimpled Manifold Model" of how neural network decision boundaries evolve during training,<ref>{{cite arXiv |eprint=2106.10151 |class=cs.LG |first1=Adi |last1=Shamir |first2=Odelia |last2=Melamed |title=The Dimpled Manifold Model of Adversarial Examples in Machine Learning |last3=BenShmuel |first3=Oriel |year=2021}}</ref> and on cryptanalytic techniques for extracting the parameters of [[neural network models]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Canales-Martínez |first1=Isaac A. |title=Advances in Cryptology – EUROCRYPT 2024 |last2=Chávez-Saab |first2=Jorge |last3=Hambitzer |first3=Anna |last4=Rodríguez-Henríquez |first4=Francisco |last5=Satpute |first5=Nitin |last6=Shamir |first6=Adi |publisher=Springer |year=2024 |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=14653 |chapter=Polynomial Time Cryptanalytic Extraction of Neural Network Models |doi=10.1007/978-3-031-58734-4_1}}</ref>

In March 2019, Shamir was unable to attend the [[RSA Conference]] in San Francisco, where he traditionally appeared on the Cryptographers' Panel, after his application for a US visa went unanswered for two months; addressing the conference by video, he suggested that the research community reconsider where it holds its scientific conferences.<ref>{{cite web |last=Spring |first=Tom |date=March 6, 2019 |title=RSA Conference 2019: Cryptographers' Panel Decries Adi Shamir's Visa Issues |url=https://threatpost.com/rsa-conference-2019-cryptographers-panel-decries-adi-shamirs-visa-issues/142533/ |access-date=July 13, 2026 |website=Threatpost}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

Beyond cryptography, Shamir has made contributions to computer science more broadly, such as finding the first [[linear time]] algorithm for [[2-satisfiability]]<ref name="EIS76">{{citation|first1=S.|last1=Even|author1-link=Shimon Even|first2=A.|last2=Itai|first3=A.|last3=Shamir|author3-link=Adi Shamir|title=On the complexity of time table and multi-commodity flow problems|journal=[[SIAM Journal on Computing]]|volume=5|issue=4|year=1976|pages=691–703|doi=10.1137/0205048}}.</ref> and proving, building on work of [[Carsten Lund]], [[Lance Fortnow]], Howard Karloff, and [[Noam Nisan]], that the [[computational complexity theory|complexity classes]] [[PSPACE]] and [[IP (complexity)|IP]] are equal.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Shamir |first=Adi |date=October 1992 |title=IP = PSPACE |journal=[[Journal of the ACM]] |volume=39 |issue=4 |pages=869–877 |doi=10.1145/146585.146609}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Shen |first=Alexander |date=October 1992 |title=IP = PSPACE: Simplified Proof |journal=[[Journal of the ACM]] |volume=39 |issue=4 |pages=878–880 |doi=10.1145/146585.146613}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition ==
* 1983 – [[Erdős Prize]] of the Israel Mathematical Society.<ref>{{cite web |title=Erdős Prize |url=https://www.imu.org.il/erdos-prize |access-date=July 13, 2026 |publisher=[[Israel Mathematical Union]]}}</ref><ref name=":0" />
* 1986 – [[IEEE W.R.G. Baker Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ieee.org/documents/baker_rl.pdf |title=IEEE W.R.G. Baker Prize Paper Award Recipients |publisher=[[IEEE]] |access-date={{Format date|2011|2|5}} |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://www.webcitation.org/5yCQiCmPi?url=http://www.ieee.org/documents/baker_rl.pdf |archive-date=2011-04-25 }}</ref>
* 1990 – UAP Scientific Prize (le Prix scientifique UAP ([[Union des Assurances de Paris]])).{{clarify|date=February 2019}}
*  1992 – [[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]] (Vaticans [[Pius XI Gold Medal|PIUS XI Gold Medal]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pas.va/content/accademia/en/about/medal.html|title=Pius XI Medal|website=www.pas.va|access-date=2019-02-21|archive-date=2014-12-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141231094609/http://www.pas.va/content/accademia/en/about/medal.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*  1996 – [[Paris Kanellakis Theory and Practice Award]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://awards.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=8526038&srt=all&aw=147&ao=KANELLAK |title=ACM Award Citation / Adi Shamir |access-date=2009-02-17 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090406004638/http://awards.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=8526038&srt=all&aw=147&ao=KANELLAK |archive-date=2009-04-06 }}</ref>
*  1998 – Elected to the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]].<ref name=":0" />
* 2000 – [[IEEE Koji Kobayashi Computers and Communications Award]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ieee.org/documents/kobayashi_rl.pdf |title=IEEE Koji Kobayashi Computers and Communications Award Recipients |publisher=[[IEEE]] |access-date={{Format date|2011|2|15}} |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101124233804/http://ieee.org/documents/kobayashi_rl.pdf |archive-date=2010-11-24 }}</ref>
* 2002 – [[Association for Computing Machinery|ACM]] [[Turing Award]], together with [[Ronald Rivest|Rivest]] and [[Leonard Adleman|Adleman]], in recognition of his contributions to cryptography.<ref name=":0">{{cite web | title=A.M. Turing Award Winners by Year | website=Association for Computing Machinery (ACM)|publisher=[[Association for Computing Machinery]] | url=https://amturing.acm.org/byyear.cfm | access-date=2026-07-05}}</ref>
* 2004 – Fellow of the [[International Association for Cryptologic Research]].<ref name=":0" />
* 2005 – Elected to the United States [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=":0" />
*  2008 – [[Israel Prize]] for computer sciences.<ref>{{Cite web | title = Israel Prize Official Site (in Hebrew) - Recipient's C.V. | url = http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashsch/AdiShamir/CvAdiShamir.htm | url-status = live | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120910075244/http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashsch/AdiShamir/CvAdiShamir.htm | archive-date = 2012-09-10 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | title = Israel Prize Official Site (in Hebrew) - Judges' Rationale for Grant to Recipient | url = http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashsch/AdiShamir/NsAdiShamir.htm | url-status = live | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120910072852/http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashsch/AdiShamir/NsAdiShamir.htm | archive-date = 2012-09-10 }}</ref>
*  2009 – Honorary DMath (Doctor of Mathematics) degree from the [[University of Waterloo]]<ref>{{Cite web | title = Presentation of the honorary degree at the Fall 2009 Convcation | url = http://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/co/research/files/award_files/AShamircitation.pdf | access-date = {{Format date|2011|10|31}} | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110924021934/https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/co/research/files/award_files/AShamircitation.pdf | archive-date = 2011-09-24 }}</ref>
* 2017 – (33rd) [[Japan Prize]] in the field of Electronics, Information and Communication for his contribution to [[information security]] through pioneering research on cryptography.<ref>{{cite web|title=Laureates of the Japan Prize|url=http://www.japanprize.jp/en/prize_past_2017_prize01.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170204171819/http://www.japanprize.jp/en/prize_past_2017_prize01.html|archive-date=2017-02-04}}</ref>
*  2018 –&nbsp;[[Foreign Member of the Royal Society]] (ForMemRS) for substantial contribution to the improvement of natural knowledge.<ref name=formemrs>{{cite web|title=Adi Shamir ForMemRS|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/adi-shamir-13842/|website=royalsociety.org|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|access-date=2018-07-22|author=Anon|year=2018}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|"All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." --{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/|title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies|date=2016-11-11}}}}</ref>
* 2019 – Elected a Member of the [[American Philosophical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |date=May 2019 |title=APS Announces 2019 Class of New Members |url=https://www.amphilsoc.org/blog/aps-announces-2019-class-new-members |access-date=July 13, 2026 |publisher=[[American Philosophical Society]]}}</ref>
* 2022 – Elected an International Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Adi Shamir |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/math/adi-shamir |access-date=July 13, 2026 |website=Weizmann Institute of Science}}</ref>
* 2024 – [[Wolf Prize in Mathematics]] for his fundamental contributions to Mathematical Cryptography.
* 2025 – [[Levchin Prize]] for his contributions to Real World Cryptography.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Levchin Prize for Real-World Cryptography |url=https://rwc.iacr.org/LevchinPrize/ |access-date=2025-03-26 |website=rwc.iacr.org}}</ref>
